paper_topic: Data-free transition-spectrum winsorization for Mamba long-context generalization
anchor_paper: Mamba Modulation / calibrated scaling (Lu et al., 2025)

nodes.text: State space models (SSMs) have emerged as an efficient alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling, offering linear-time complexity in sequence length (Gu et al., 2021; Gu & Dao, 2023).
Mamba (Gu & Dao, 2023) and its successor Mamba2 (Dao & Gu, 2024) achieve competitive performance with Transformers while enabling efficient processing of long sequences.

However, when evaluated on contexts significantly longer than their training distribution, these models exhibit severe perplexity degradation—Mamba2-1.3B's perplexity explodes from 9.31 at 2K tokens to over 1400 at 64K tokens.
nodes.display_label: Mamba PPL explodes at long contexts

nodes.text: This long-context failure stems from extreme eigenvalues in the transition spectrum.
Eigenvalues near 1 cause state explosion as historical information accumulates without sufficient decay, while eigenvalues near 0 lead to premature context loss.
Prior work has addressed this through calibrated scaling (Lu et al., 2025), which determines optimal per-layer scaling factors via forward passes on representative data.
While effective (achieving PPL@64K of 4.72), this approach requires calibration data that may not always be available.
Constant scaling provides a data-free alternative but applies uniform modifications to all channels, degrading short-context performance (PPL@2K increases from 9.31 to 11.25).

We propose transition-spectrum winsorization, a data-free method that clips only the extreme eigenvalues in each layer's spectrum while preserving the mid-spectrum.

By targeting channels with eigenvalues outside the [q, 1−q] percentile range, our method modifies only 17.5% of channels while achieving better performance than constant scaling on both short and long contexts.
A data-free method for Mamba long-context extension via transition-spectrum winsorization, achieving PPL@64K of 11.44 (13% better than constant scaling) without requiring calibration data.
Empirical demonstration that targeted clipping of extreme eigenvalues (17.5% of channels) outperforms uniform scaling (100% of channels), with lower short-context regression (+6.8% vs +20.8%).
Mechanism analysis revealing that extreme effective eigenvalues are driven by input-dependent ∆t dynamics rather than static A outliers, motivating future work on input-dependent interventions.

observations:
FA0181 is a method paper with two cleanly paired Prior_Work to Limitation pivots. Para 1 (N1-N5) is Context. Although para 1 contains a 'However' (N3: Mamba PPL explodes at long contexts), this is paper-theme-aligned — the paper IS about long-context generalization, so this 'However' frames the field-level problem the paper itself studies, not a critique of any specific named Prior_Work method. N4-N5 elaborate the mechanistic cause (extreme eigenvalues, near-1 explode and near-0 forget) — still Context.

Para 2 introduces the actual Prior_Work to be critiqued: N6 (calibrated scaling, Lu et al., 2025) is the anchor with a 'While effective... but' contrast to N7 (calibrated scaling needs calibration data). N8 introduces a second baseline (constant scaling) and is split from its critique clause N8lim (uniform modifications degrade short context) using Pass 3 Case C, giving N8lim a clean PW source (N8).

The Method block (N9-N10) proposes transition-spectrum winsorization with the [q, 1-q] percentile-based clipping mechanism. Three Contributions (C1-C3) close the intro and are fed by N10. Two addresses edges connect contributions to limitations: C1 (data-free method, no calibration) addresses N7 (calibrated scaling needs data), and C2 (targeted 17.5% beats uniform 100%) addresses N8lim (constant scaling degrades short context). C3 (mechanism analysis of input-dependent dynamics) is exploratory and does not have a clean lexical bridge to a single Limitation. Topology shows N10 as contribution-fork.
